title: Linear response functions from inhomogeneous dynamical mean-field theory
abstract: We present a method for calculating static lattice susceptibilities with inhomogeneous dynamical mean-field theory. The method utilizes the response of the system to an external field and thereby circumvents two-particle vertex functions. We demonstrate the success of our approach for the magnetic susceptibility of the square-lattice Hubbard model using the numerical renormalization group as an impurity solver and show that it compares well with the results obtained using the standard vertex approach. As it avoids vertex functions and is compatible with virtually any impurity solver, our method is able to reach low temperatures that are hard to access with other methods.
summary: This paper introduces an improved method using inhomogeneous Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (iDMFT) to calculate lattice susceptibilities by employing linear response theory. This approach bypasses the computationally prohibitive calculation of two-particle vertex functions inherent in standard methods. The results confirm its accuracy while significantly expanding the accessible temperature range for studying magnetic instabilities in correlated electron models.
main_problem: The primary goal is calculating static lattice susceptibilities ($\chi$) for strongly correlated electron systems, specifically addressing the computational difficulty of standard vertex function approaches.
main_result: The proposed inhomogeneous Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (iDMFT) method successfully calculates $\chi$ by utilizing linear response theory to an external field, showing good agreement with established vertex methods while enabling access to very low temperatures.
method: The authors derive the susceptibility using a linear response expansion in a small applied magnetic field ($B$), which avoids explicit calculation of two-particle vertex functions and is compatible with various impurity solvers like NRG.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Hubbard model, typically analyzed on a 2D square lattice. The theoretical framework involves mapping the lattice problem onto an impurity problem solved via DMFT/iDMFT techniques.
key_observables: Static lattice magnetic susceptibility ($\chi_q$ or $\chi_i$), which measures the system's response to external magnetic perturbations.
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U$), temperature ($ eta^{-1}$), and doping level ($n$). The analysis compares results across different interaction regimes.
main_assumptions: The method relies on expanding in the applied field $B$ (linear response) to circumvent complex vertex calculations. For thermodynamic limits, a specific resummation scheme is necessary for divergence.
figures_summary: Figures compare real-space and momentum-space susceptibility ($\chi_i, \chi_q$) across different methods (iDMFT vs. DMFT vertex) at various temperatures and interaction strengths, demonstrating convergence after applying the appropriate resummation.
paper_structure: The paper develops a novel iDMFT formalism for $\chi$ via linear response theory, proves its equivalence to standard approaches using Ward identities, and applies it numerically to benchmark results against established DMFT calculations across different parameter regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the use of linear response theory in strongly correlated systems is a powerful general technique for calculating susceptibilities that can inform open quantum system dynamics or magnetic responses in AMO contexts.
